conventions.convention: The penalty uses the exact intrinsic derivative/Slobodeckij Hilbert norm on the ball, with the integer derivative norm at s=3. Equivalent Fourier norms are used for estimates, not substituted into the penalty pairing.

Conductivities equal 1 outside a fixed interior ball. Neumann currents and boundary voltages have boundary mean zero; the sequence observation is centered by subtracting the background NtD map. Harmonic degrees start at ℓ=1 with multiplicity 2ℓ+1.
The Liouville potential is q=(Δ√σ)/√σ, the Schrödinger operator is −Δ+q, null CGO phases sum to −ξ, and the boundary identity uses bilinear pairing without complex conjugation.

The boundary data space is H¹/H¹₀ with its quotient norm, identified with the finite-chart W^{1/2,2} space up to norm equivalence. Quotienting further by constants requires functionals to annihilate constants.

The conjugate is H(q)=sup_{s≥0}(ψ(s)−qs). The logarithmic index is continued constantly above a sufficiently small positive cutoff; quadratic Bregman rates convert to norm rates by halving the logarithmic exponent.

At the nominal endpoint α comparable to δ^p, the effective noise/tolerance term must be O(δ^p log(1/δ)^{−ν}); the ordinary deterministic noise bound alone is insufficient for the universal abstract assertion.
Frozen updates start at n=1 and freeze at x_{n−1}. The parameter sequence is fixed independently of noise, and stopping uses the last index whose ρ_n remains above the target.

The EIT augmentation uses coefficient coordinates relative to σ₀, X=Z=V×Y with the sum norm, P(a,z)=(0,z), and a convex indicator enforcing the physical conductivity class. Frozen rates additionally require LR<c_tcr<1/√20.

load_bearing.statement: On the stated collared conductivity class, the explicit observation augmentation satisfies the joint and frozen structural interfaces with p=2, exact quadratic Bregman distance, b=3/4, and logarithmic source exponent ν=(s₂−s₁)(2s₁−3)/(s₂−1); frozen rates additionally require the stated small-neighborhood and parameter conditions.

For the fixed collared positive H^s conductivity class, 5/2<s<7/2, the H¹ conductivity difference is at most C[log(3+δ⁻¹)]^{−(s−3/2)} for δ>0, where δ is the centered NtD column-sequence distance. Zero distance implies equality.

For 5/2<s<7/2 and s<t<2s−1, the exact intrinsic penalty pairing has cutoff bound C2^{J(2s−t−1)}‖σ−σ†‖_{H¹}+C2^{−J(t−s)}‖σ−σ†‖_{s,Ω}. The stated conditional H¹ modulus yields the VSC with coefficient 3/4 and source modulus raised to 2(t−s)/(t−1).

Compactly supported q∈H^{1/2+τ}, 0<τ<1, with the stated norm bound admits CGO solutions for every sufficiently large null phase, with remainder bounds O(|ζ|⁻¹) in H^{1/2}, O(|ζ|^{−τ/2}) in L∞, and the displayed H² bound.
For b≥1 and Q∈H^{−1/2}(R³), the integral over |ξ|≤b of ⟨ξ⟩⁻¹‖e^{−iξ·x}Q‖²_{H^{−1/2}} is at most Cb²‖Q‖²_{H^{−1/2}}.
Under the stated factorization, VSC, projection-coupling and admitted approximate-minimum hypotheses, s_δ+(1−b)αe_δ≤d_δ+αψ(C_*s_δ).
Under the stated Taylor, VSC, penalty, compatibility and linked-parameter hypotheses, S_{n+1}+α_nE_{n+1}≤d_n+α_nψ(C̄S_{n+1}), with the two displayed conjugate bounds.

On the stated bounded connected C¹ domain, trace induces a bounded isomorphism H¹/H¹₀→W^{1/2,2}(∂Ω), also after quotienting by constants; continuous linear functionals descend exactly when they annihilate constants, preserving their quotient dual norm.

concerns.concern: The Remark says Corollary 11 reports an exponent 'divided by the source parameter' p̃, and [F5] explicitly attributes ν_paper/p̃ to that source. The cited [arXiv v1, Corollary 11, printed p. 24](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18704v1#S3) instead prints denominator (s₁−1)p and fixes p=2; p̃ occurs separately in α comparable to δ^{p̃}. Thus the attributed norm exponent is ν_paper/2, not ν_paper/p̃. The cached primary-source transcription at research/inverse-problems-knot-theory-all-109-2026-10-19-owner-eit-prerequisites-independent-review-round1/sources/kaltenbacher-read-passages.txt agrees. This is a false numerical source attribution, although the independently proved local ν/2 rate conclusions are unaffected.
